title: forbidden_pattern and no_cycles ignore #[cfg(test)], drowning real signal
description:
Adopting vidhi/language-rules/rust.toml into yojana (commit cc9c4e5) surfaced one root cause producing three separate false-positive classes: sutra's AST pattern matching and import-graph analysis both treat `#[cfg(test)]` code as production code.

Measured on yojana (24 files, 674 symbols), scope `src/`:

- `no-unwrap`: 417 matches, **415 inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`**. 2 genuine production hits. 99.5% noise.
- `no-clone-driven-dev`: 57 matches, 21 in `tests::`.
- builtin `no_cycles` (blocking): reports `src/tools/arc.rs -> src/tools/task.rs`. The cycle is **entirely test-only** — `arc.rs:197 use crate::tools::task;` sits inside the cfg(test) mod starting at line 194, and `task.rs:432 use crate::tools::arc;` likewise. There is no production cycle. A blocking builtin is reporting a violation that does not exist.

Sutra already has the data needed to fix this: violation records carry `enclosing_symbol` values like `tests::json_round_trip`, so the test provenance is known at report time and simply isn't acted on.

This matters beyond noise. clippy handles the same case correctly via `allow-unwrap-in-tests`, which makes sutra strictly *less* accurate than the lint it is meant to front-run at edit time. That inverts the value proposition: the layer with blocking teeth is the one with worse precision. Until this is fixed, `no-unwrap` cannot honestly be promoted past advisory in any Rust crate that uses inline test modules — which is idiomatic Rust, so effectively all of them.

Rust-specific but the shape generalises; Dart's `@visibleForTesting` and `test/` layout will want the same treatment.

acceptance_criteria.text: forbidden_pattern violations inside #[cfg(test)] modules are excluded by default
no_cycles ignores import edges that originate inside #[cfg(test)] modules
Opt-in escape hatch exists for rules that genuinely should cover test code (e.g. include_tests = true per constraint)
Re-running violations on yojana reports 2 no-unwrap hits (db.rs, main.rs pre-fix) and zero no_cycles violations
Behaviour documented in the forbidden_pattern reference section of vidhi-sutra-adopt/SKILL.md

decisions.decision: Filter test-scope findings at report time against a production-edge set rather than pruning test edges from the DD graph before ingest
decisions.rationale: Keeps include_tests a per-constraint property. The DD engine maintains one shared graph used for violations, cycles and blast radius; pruning would bake the setting into the graph, so supporting include_tests=true and false in the same run would need two graphs and two workers.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Prune test edges in db.import_edges() before ingest — simplest diff, but makes include_tests all-or-nothing per workspace and silently changes blast-radius/trace results, which are unrelated to constraints and legitimately want the full graph.

decisions.decision: Exclude include_tests from constraint identity (blake3 id), matching ratchet
decisions.rationale: Toggling enforcement scope on an existing rule must not orphan its waivers or ratchet registration; scope is in identity because differently-scoped rules are semantically distinct rules, whereas include_tests modulates one rule.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Include it in the hash for strict semantic identity — correct in the abstract, but every adopter flipping the flag would silently lose their waiver history, which is the exact churn the ratchet registry exists to prevent.

decisions.decision: Guard paths drop test edges unconditionally instead of honouring per-constraint include_tests
decisions.rationale: The guard derives proposed edges by parsing pending content and has no cheap path to per-constraint re-evaluation; an edit-time deny while writing test wiring is the precise failure this task was filed for. The review path still enforces include_tests fully.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Thread include_tests through the guard's edge derivation — more faithful, but doubles the guard's per-edit work for a flag expected to be rare, and the analysis layer already catches the case without blocking the edit.

execution_record:
Two mechanisms behind one flag, because the two failure classes have different data paths:

- Pattern kinds: new `LanguageAdapter::test_line_ranges(ctx)` hook (empty default, Rust override). `patterns.rs` caches ranges per path across the per-constraint loop and drops matches inside them.
- Edge kinds: new `imports.is_test` column (migration 0053) populated in `rust::parse` from the same ranges, plus `db::production_import_edges()`.

Design call worth recording: the DD graph is left whole and filtering happens at *finding* time, not by pruning edges before ingest. Pruning was the obvious move but would have made `include_tests` a property of the graph rather than of a constraint, forcing two graphs to support both settings simultaneously.

`no_cycles` needed more than a boolean skip — a cycle can be partly real. It now re-runs `worker::compute_sccs` (made `pub(crate)`) over production edges restricted to the reported cycle's nodes and emits surviving sub-SCCs. Verified the contract is unchanged for pure-production cycles: both paths sort node ids, so `from_path`/`to_path`/detail round-trip identically.

Two contract traps caught before landing:
1. First cut filtered the Resolved-delta loop the same way as the active loop, which suppressed *every* resolution — a resolved edge is by definition absent from the current graph, so it's absent from production_edges too. Correct predicate: skip only when the pair is still present but now test-only.
2. `attribute_marks_test` initially treated any `cfg` containing `test` as test scope, which would have muted rules under `#[cfg(not(test))]` and `#[cfg(feature = "test-helpers")]`. Now bails on `not(` and on any string literal — errs toward over-reporting.

Verification: 1479 tests pass, clippy warning profile byte-identical to baseline. Measured against yojana HEAD with a throwaway harness (removed before commit, not committed): no-unwrap 413 -> 0 (confirmed all 413 are test code by re-running with include_tests), no_cycles 1 -> 0, no-clone-driven-dev 57 -> 36 — the 36 exactly matches the task's recorded 57-minus-21-in-tests split.

Deviation from acceptance criterion 4: it expected 2 surviving no-unwrap hits in db.rs and main.rs; actual is 0. Not a filter bug — yojana fixed both production unwraps in commits 3cdae7e/0b3ff34 after cc9c4e5. Independently confirmed: zero `.unwrap()` calls remain anywhere in yojana/src outside a `#[cfg(test)]` boundary.

Known gap filed as sutra/292: Rust `tests/*.rs` integration tests and all Dart test code are still undetected. Left out deliberately — a blanket path-based exclusion would silently kill rules deliberately scoped to `tests/`, and that design question deserved its own decision rather than a snap call here.

Docs: `docs/constraints-map.md` (new "Test scope" section) and `vidhi-sutra-adopt/SKILL.md` (committed separately in the vidhi repo as 3f9979f).
root_cause: Constraint evaluation had no concept of test scope: `patterns.rs` ran tree-sitter queries over whole files, and the import graph fed to the DD engine came from `db.import_edges()`, which is every resolved import row regardless of where it sits. Nothing downstream distinguished a `use` inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` from a production one, so test code — which exists precisely to exercise the constructs production rules forbid — was scored as production. The `enclosing_symbol` field on findings already carried the evidence (`tests::json_round_trip`) but was only ever a display string; no code branched on it.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review of c483406 (base 537a598) — verdict: needs-attention (request changes).

[high] cfg_attr(test, ...) misclassified as test-only — src/parser/rust.rs attribute_marks_test. It accepts any attribute text starting with "cfg" then containing a bare `test` token, so `#[cfg_attr(test, derive(...))]` on a production item marks the whole item test-only. patterns.rs then skips all matches in that range and rust::parse marks its imports is_test=1, so production code silently bypasses blocking forbidden_pattern / forbidden_dep / no_cycles. Same class: the `not(` guard is a literal substring check, so `#[cfg(not (test))]` (space) also falls through to bare-token matching and is classified as test. Both fail in the unsafe direction, opposite to the stated conservative intent. Fix: match the cfg predicate structurally; treat cfg_attr as production unless it expands to cfg(test); handle `not` structurally. Regression tests for both.

[high] Existing indexes keep old test imports as production — migrations/0053_import_is_test.sql:4 adds is_test with DEFAULT 0, but is_test is only populated at parse time, and pipeline.rs:208-214 skips reparse when content_hash is unchanged. An upgraded workspace therefore keeps pre-migration cfg(test) imports flagged production indefinitely, with nothing in constraint evaluation detecting it — AC4 can read false on any pre-existing index. Fix: invalidate Rust file parse state as part of the migration (bump an index schema version in the skip predicate, or clear content_hash for Rust files).

[medium] Production self-loop cycles dropped by the narrowing — src/constraints/check.rs, the new `.filter(|scc| scc.len() > 1)`. worker.rs:117-119 derives cycle nodes from transitive-closure self-loops, so a genuine production self-edge (a file importing a path that resolves back to itself) was previously reportable as a one-node cycle and is now unconditionally discarded. Fix: keep singleton SCCs when production_edges contains (id, id); test both the production self-loop and its test-only suppression.

[medium] External-crate constraints still evaluate cfg(test) imports — db::unresolved_imports_with_files (src/db/mod.rs) selects no is_test column, and the SingleFile external query in check.rs:602-606 likewise. check_import_items has no include_tests signal, so forbidden_external/confined_external still fire blocking on a crate used only inside #[cfg(test)]. The commit message claims test code is excluded from *every* constraint kind; that is not yet true for import-derived external rules. Directly blocks yojana/44 (re-adding rusqlite confined_external). Fix: return is_test and filter unless the matching constraint sets include_tests.

[dismissed] Codex flagged AC5 (vidhi-sutra-adopt/SKILL.md) unmet. It is met — documented in vidhi commit 3f9979f, a separate repo Codex could not see.

Orchestrator notes: all four findings verified against the source, not taken on report. The RawConn edge query hardcoding `is_test = 0` regardless of include_tests is the documented guard-path trade-off, not a defect. sutra_review on the range: risk 0.954 (blast radius/churn/complexity all saturated); its one blocking no_cycles hit is sutra's own pre-existing src/tools/* cycle, unrelated.

edges.note: no-unwrap severity cannot be decided until cfg(test) violations are excluded — blocking at 415 false positives is unusable
